source.title: Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible
source.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset and David Brown
source.edition: CCEL expanded electronic edition of the 1871 public-domain text

entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: Ps 66:1-20 . The writer invites all men to unite in praise, cites some striking occasions for it, promises special acts of thanksgiving, and celebrates God's great mercy.

entries.heading: 2. his name
entries.text: 2. his name --as in Ps 29:2 . make his praise glorious --literally, "place honor, His praise," or, "as to His praise"; that is, let His praise be such as will glorify Him, or, be honorable to Him.
3, 4. A specimen of the praise. How terrible --(Compare Ps 65:8 ). submit --(Compare Margin ), show a forced subjection ( Ps 18:44 ), produced by terror.
5, 6. The terrible works illustrated in Israel's history ( Ex 14:21 ). By this example let rebels be admonished.
8, 9. Here is, perhaps, cited a case of recent deliverance.

entries.heading: 9. holdeth . . . in life
entries.text: 9. holdeth . . . in life --literally, "putteth our soul in life"; that is, out of danger ( Ps 30:3; 49:15 ). to be moved --(Compare Ps 10:6; 55:22 ).
10-12. Out of severe trials, God had brought them to safety (compare Isa 48:10; 1Pe 1:7 ).

entries.heading: 11. affliction
entries.text: 11. affliction --literally, "pressure," or, as in Ps 55:3 , "oppression," which, laid on the loins --the seat of strength ( De 33:11 ), enfeebles the frame.

entries.heading: 12. men to ride over our heads
entries.text: 12. men to ride over our heads --made us to pass. through fire, &c.--figures describing prostration and critical dangers (compare Isa 43:2; Eze 36:12 ). wealthy --literally, "overflowing," or, "irrigated," and hence fertile.
13-15. These full and varied offerings constitute the payment of vows ( Le 22:18-23 ).

entries.heading: 15. I will offer
entries.text: 15. I will offer --literally, "make to ascend," alluding to the smoke of burnt offering, which explains the use of "incense." incense --elsewhere always denoting the fumes of aromatics.

16-20. With these he unites his public thanks, inviting those who fear God ( Ps 60:4; 61:5 , His true worshippers) to hear. He vindicates his sincerity, inasmuch as God would not hear hypocrites, but had heard him.

entries.heading: 17. he was extolled with my tongue
entries.text: 17. he was extolled with my tongue --literally, "exaltation (was) under my tongue," as a place of deposit, whence it proceeded; that is, honoring God was habitual.

entries.heading: 18. If I regard iniquity in my heart
entries.text: 18. If I regard iniquity in my heart --literally, "see iniquity with pleasure."
